audit_findings.title: FY2025 interest expense is not a sustainable debt-cost anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $720.925 million principal subject to anticipated repayment in 2027 and 2029; valuation impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher refinancing interest would reduce equity-level OE beginning in the forecast period because interest expense is retained in OE while debt is not deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s predominantly fixed-rate debt structure has reduced its exposure to interest rate increases that could adversely affect its earnings and cash flows, but the Company remains exposed to changes in market interest rates reflected in the fair value of the debt and to the risk that the Company may need to refinance maturing debt with new debt at a higher rate.
audit_findings.explanation: No refinancing-cost error is presently demonstrated because future coupons are unknown. The exposure is forward-looking but important: $472.800 million bearing 2.84% has a December 2027 anticipated repayment date and $248.125 million bearing 3.734% has a March 2029 anticipated repayment date. Mechanically growing FY2025 OE without changing interest expense could overstate value if either tranche refinances at a higher rate.
audit_findings.action: Model the two repayment dates using documented refinancing-rate sensitivities, recalculate after-tax equity OE from 2027 onward, and replace the sensitivity with actual terms when refinancing occurs.

audit_findings.title: The LPH transaction may be mismatched between OE and the stake bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $88.958 million carrying value versus the rounded $89.0 million bridge, net of a $5.0 million CECL allowance; $18.395 million foreign-investment deferred-tax liability and $8.770 million FY2025 noncash investment income require reconciliation
audit_findings.mechanism: LPH affects both normalized OE through sale gain, credit provision, preference-share interest and equity-method income, and the equity bridge through the separately added investment and related tax or credit claims.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company received proceeds of $ 107.7 million in the fiscal first quarter 2025 and recognized a gain of $ 97.2 million in Investment (income) expense on the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest $89.0 million bridge agrees closely with the filed $88.958 million carrying value, so a bridge-amount error is not demonstrated. The record nevertheless lacks the OE adjustment ledger and does not establish whether preference-share interest, equity-method income, the $92.485 million net sale gain, CECL effects and the associated deferred tax were treated consistently. Any double counting would overstate value, while an excessive purge could understate it; materiality cannot be established from the supplied reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile reported FY2025 net income to the $96.4 million OE anchor line by line and reconcile the $89.0 million bridge to preference shares, ordinary shares, the CECL allowance and the portion of the foreign-investment deferred-tax liability attributable to LPH; then rerun if any item appears in both OE and the bridge or is omitted from both.

audit_findings.title: Restricted Ad Fund activity may contaminate common-equity owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.910 million FY2025 operating-cash-flow drag from Ad Fund asset-and-liability movements and a $13.926 million FY2025 advertising-expense-over-fee gap
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted Ad Fund timing movements can enter consolidated income and operating cash flow even though the related resources are unavailable to common equity; restricted cash could also improperly enter the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to the Company’s franchise agreements, use of Ad Fund contributions is restricted to advertising, public relations, merchandising, similar activities, and administrative expenses to increase sales and further enhance the public reputation of the Wingstop brand.
audit_findings.explanation: The $127.455 million bridge cash equals the latest filed unrestricted cash balance, so no restricted-cash bridge error is demonstrated. The OE numerator remains unresolved. The filed $16.910 million cash-flow movement equals 17.5% of the $96.4 million anchor, making an unneutralized timing item reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation. Both identified FY2025 effects reduced reported earnings or operating cash flow, so retaining them would understate value.
audit_findings.action: Trace Ad Fund fees, recognized expense, accrued spending, receivables, payables and restricted cash through the FY2025 OE calculation; neutralize only timing movements, retain Wingstop-borne advertising costs, and rerun all scenarios if any portion of the $16.910 million movement entered the anchor.

audit_findings.title: Technology implementation costs are recurring unless the evidence proves otherwise
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.773 million pretax, $5.147 million after tax at the filed 24% adjustment rate, and approximately $3.06 per share of base value if fully omitted
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back implementation expense or related amortization increases anchor OE while the forecast simultaneously credits growth supported by those technology investments.
audit_findings.evidence: We have core information systems in place that, together with focused investments we have made and continue to make in technology (including our proprietary digital platform), we believe are designed to scale and support our future growth plans.
audit_findings.explanation: Recurring implementation-related charges are demonstrated across reporting periods, but their inclusion in the $96.4 million anchor is not shown. If the entire $5.839 million expense and $0.934 million amortization were improperly removed, the computed base value would fall from $65.10 to about $62.04 per share and the bull value from $71.74 to about $68.32. Both remain well below the $109.205 market price, so this item alone does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE adjustment ledger, retain the $5.839 million implementation expense and $0.934 million amortization unless a specifically documented nonrecurring portion is isolated, and rerun the valuation if they were added back.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a one-time building-disposal loss
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.534 million pretax, $4.966 million after tax at the filed 24% adjustment rate, and approximately $2.95 per share of base value if retained
audit_findings.mechanism: A one-time disposal loss left in anchor OE is capitalized through every forecast year; the related sale proceeds could separately affect bridge cash.
audit_findings.evidence: (Gain) loss on disposal of assets was $6.5 million related to a loss on sale of an office building during the fiscal first quarter 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The $6.534 million nonrecurring building loss is demonstrated, but the record does not show whether it remains in the $96.4 million anchor. A full after-tax correction would increase computed base value from $65.10 to about $68.05 per share and bull value from $71.74 to about $75.04, still well below the $109.205 market price. It therefore cannot change the present valuation conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Confirm in the OE ledger that the $6.534 million loss and its tax effect were removed exactly once, trace the $17.330 million sale proceeds into ending cash, and rerun only if the loss remains or the proceeds were double counted.
